days.title: Canyon Depths and Hiking Trails
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Gola di Gorropu
stops.detail: The Gorropu Gorge, with its walls up to over 500 m in height and a width that varies from 4 meters at the narrowest points to reaching several dozen in others, is considered the deepest canyon in Italy and one of the deepest in Europe.

stops.name: Rio Flumineddu
stops.detail: The gorge originated following the opening of a fault and thanks to the intense erosive action caused by the waters of the Rio Flumineddu.

stops.name: Sentiero Sedda ar Bacas - Gorropu B-502
stops.detail: The canyon can be reached by following a hiking route (the Sedda ar Bacas - Gorropu B-502 trail) for experts, for which adequate equipment and possibly a guide are necessary.

days.title: Valleys, Rivers and Caves
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Grotta Su Palu
stops.detail: Upstream, before entering the gorge, the waters of the Flumineddu river gush from the rocks and create natural water basins in which it is possible to find the Sardinian trout and especially the Sardinian brook salamander: a Sardinian-Corsican endemism considered the rarest amphibian in Europe besides the Supramonte cave salamander, present in the nearby Su Palu cave.

stops.name: Valle di Oddoene
stops.detail: From the village, you take the road by car that leads through the vineyards of the Oddoene valley, at the foot of Supramonte.

stops.name: Ponte di S'Abba Arva
stops.detail: Having left the car near the S'Abba Arva bridge (there is an equipped rest area of the same name), you follow the path that winds along the river, offering panoramic views of remarkable beauty and also giving the possibility of swimming in one of the natural ponds formed by the stream.
